chunks: From him, from ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who performs sajdah on his sleeve to protect himself from the harm of heat and cold, or on his cloak when beneath it there is a coarse cloth or something else upon which sajdah is not performed. He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَذَى الْحَرِّ وَالْبَرْدِ: the harm caused by heat and cold
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لَا يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهِ: that upon which sajdah is not performed
key_terms.مِسْحٌ: a coarse cloth or fabric spread beneath

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on one's sleeve or cloak due to heat or cold?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sajdah when a person seeks protection from excessive heat or cold. It indicates that there is no harm in performing sajdah on one's sleeve or cloak in such circumstances, even if there is beneath it something upon which sajdah is ordinarily not performed.
